aliases.reason: The categorical-compactness formulation writes Hom_C(X,M_i), and the preadditive and representable-presheaf formulations write Hom_C(X,Y). The prerequisite is the collection of C-arrows with fixed endpoints. Compactness uses set-valued Hom and may need its local-smallness or universe convention, retained in the parent formulation rather than imposed on the underlying Hom-collection.

The category-fibred-in-sets formulation and the category-fibred-in-setoids formulation use exactly the same fibre category E_U: objects e of E with p(e)=U and morphisms whose p-image is id_U. Whether the fibre is discrete or a setoid is an additional distinct restriction in the two parent definitions.

A system of parameters generates an m-primary ideal, and an ideal of definition of a Noetherian local ring is equivalently an ideal with radical m. Within the stated Noetherian local context sqrt(I)=m implies I is m-primary; the common prerequisite is the m-primary-ideal predicate, not equivalence of the two different parent concepts.

The finitely presented ring-map source writes S≅R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_m). This invokes the general quotient-ring operation of a commutative unital ring by an ideal, specialized to a polynomial algebra and finitely generated relation ideal; those polynomial and finite-presentation requirements remain parent-specific.

The global-complete-intersection-algebra source presents S as k[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c). It invokes the same quotient-ring construction using ideal cosets and inherited ring operations; polynomial variables, finite relations, dimension equality and complete-intersection hypotheses are separately retained in the parent mathematical statement.
